issues.description: Method return type mismatch for PersonResource.getAllPersons(): the template declares public ResponseEntity<List<Person>> getAllPersons() and returns personService.getAll() (a List<Person>). The solution implementation declares public ResponseEntity<Set<Person>> getAllPersons() but still returns personService.getAll() which has signature List<Person> getAll(). This inconsistency between the controller return type (Set<Person>) and the service return type (List<Person>) causes a compile-time type error and confuses students about the expected collection type for the GET /persons endpoint.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return types consistent. Change the solution's PersonResource.getAllPersons() signature to return ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and return personService.getAll(), matching the PersonService.getAll() method and the template. Alternatively (less preferred for pedagogy), change PersonService.getAll() to return a Set<Person> and adjust repository/service code accordingly. Recommended: restore controller signature to ResponseEntity<List<Person>> to match the template and service.

issues.description: The Web-layer endpoint method that returns all persons is declared with different collection type identifiers across artifacts. Template repository declares the method as: public ResponseEntity<List<Person>> getAllPersons() (template: src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java lines 27-30). Solution repository declares the same method as: public ResponseEntity<java.util.Set<Person>> getAllPersons() (solution: src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java lines 27-30). The problem statement refers to the PersonResource Web Layer but does not specify a collection type. Because the template service method personService.getAll() and the template controller use List<Person>, while the solution controller uses Set<Person>, students face a naming/type mismatch for the same conceptual API method: they cannot reliably map the exercise requirements and template code to the reference solution and may encounter compilation or API-consistency confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection return type consistent across artifacts. Prefer aligning the solution to the template/service by changing the solution's PersonResource signature to: public ResponseEntity<List<Person>> getAllPersons() (and import java.util.List if necessary). Ensure all references (controller signature and any tests or documentation) match this List<Person> type so personService.getAll() return type and the controller response type are consistent.
